title: World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates, July 2026 — Phase 65 Agriculture and bioeconomy review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Agriculture and bioeconomy reporting pack. WASDE 673 updates official U.S. and world supply, use, trade, stocks, and price projections for major agricultural commodities for the July 2026 forecast vintage.
key_findings: The July projection lowered 2026/27 world total-grain ending stocks from the June vintage's 780.59 million metric tons to 771.62 million metric tons.

The July projection lowered 2026/27 U.S. total-grain ending stocks from 74.08 million metric tons to 68.90 million metric tons while increasing projected U.S. total-grain trade from 109.05 to 110.29 million metric tons.
Within U.S. wheat, July projected 2026/27 ending stocks at 722 million bushels versus 744 million in the June vintage, while holding the projected average farm price at $6.00 per bushel.
why_it_matters: Which records connect research and authorization to field adoption, production, resilience, water exposure, and comparable crop outcomes? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. The report provides a current official forecast baseline for agricultural supply and market risk, with the prior-vintage comparison needed to distinguish an updated outlook from an observed outcome.
ftfn_relevance: Adds a current bounded record to Agriculture and Bioeconomy.
Creates a reusable monthly method for tracking forecast revisions by commodity and marketing year.
Connects climate, trade, stocks, and price expectations without converting projections into realized conditions.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
WASDE figures are estimates and projections that can be revised in later vintages.
The report does not establish farm-level production, realized prices, or causal attribution.
Cross-commodity totals do not substitute for commodity- and region-specific analysis.
